theater: 德意志西部特伊托堡森林

battle.name: 巴托斯之戰
battle.theater: 德意志西部特伊托堡森林
battle.brief: 公元9年秋，羅馬總督瓦魯斯率第十七、十八、十九三個軍團自特伊托堡森林向奧斯納布呂克行軍，去赴九日一度的墟市，卻在卡爾克里塞沼地遭德意志聯軍包圍全殲。重裝步兵的巨盾、短劍與重標槍在泥濘中寸步難行，卡牌上的羅馬重步兵就此從此再無一人回國。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 公元9年的德意志，羅馬與一個尚未成形但紀律嚴明的部落聯軍，在威悉河、易北河與萊茵河之間的森林地帶對峙。羅馬一方是元老院帝國的常駐軍：上日耳曼總督普布利烏斯·昆克提利烏斯·瓦魯斯所率的第十七、十八、十九三個軍團，按當時編制每團約五千五百名步兵，另有數十支輔助步兵大隊、努米底亞與色雷斯騎兵大隊，以及敘利亞弓手，輔助軍是這支部隊人數最多也最難駕馭的部分。德意志一方是切羅西人、馬西人、卡蒂人、布魯克特里人、肖伊人、弗里斯蘭人等部落拼成的聯軍，由阿米尼烏斯實際統率，各首領保留本部指揮權，聯軍沒有羅馬式的後勤與工程保障。值得注意的是，聯軍中不少部落是羅馬的「盟友」，依條約提供兵員與人質，戰事正是在這種一半盟友、一半敵人的模糊關係中展開。羅馬的目標是行政兼軍事：修路、清點人口、徵稅、把首領的裁決權收歸帝國。聯軍的目標則是把羅馬的使節與軍隊趕出易北河下游，保住森林、牧場與河谷的傳統領域。
countriesEn: In the Germany of AD 9, Rome and a loose tribal confederation that had not yet become a state but was already tightly disciplined faced each other across the forests between the Weser, the Elbe and the Rhine. On the Roman side stood the permanent army of the senatorial empire: the Seventeenth, Eighteenth and Nineteenth legions under the governor of Upper Germany, Publius Quinctilius Varus, each of about five thousand five hundred men at the period establishment, backed by a number of auxiliary infantry cohorts, Numidian and Thracian cavalry alae, and Syrian archers; the auxiliaries were the largest and least reliable part of this force. On the German side stood a coalition built out of the Cherusci, Marsi, Chatti, Bructeri, Chauci and Frisians, commanded in practice by Arminius while each chieftain kept command of his own contingent; the coalition had no Roman-style logistics and no field engineering. It matters that many of these tribes were Roman allies who supplied men and hostages by treaty, so the war unfolded in the blurred zone where ally and enemy overlap. Rome's aim was administrative and military at once: roads, censuses, taxes, and the transfer of the chiefs' jurisdiction to the empire. The coalition's aim was to drive Roman envoys and soldiers back out of the lower Elbe and to keep the forests, pastures and river valleys that the tribes had always held.
people: 瓦魯斯是這場戰爭的羅馬主角。他是老派羅馬貴族的末代代表之一，出身貴族世家，歷任公職，最後被奧古斯都派往德意志收拾前任留下的行政與軍務；上任後他把整個行省的人口、土地與稅收重新登記，也帶來帝國對部落首領那套先談判、後徵稅的作風，許多德意志人對他的仇恨來自這套程序，而不是他的戰術。真正決定戰局的是阿米尼烏斯：他本人在羅馬的輔助軍中服役多年，受過羅馬式訓練，熟悉軍隊編制、值勤節奏、糧秣分配與行軍縱隊的弱點，羅馬人給他騎兵訓練，甚至讓他率領一支輔助分遣隊，因此他對羅馬的了解來自內行，而非情報。他以為聯軍募兵的名義取得羅馬的武器與糧食，用羅馬式紀律武裝起聯軍，再選定地形、安排襲擊，把羅馬引入自己選定的沼澤地帶。另一位關鍵人物是馬科曼尼王馬羅布杜斯：他拒絕加入聯軍，反而率部眾向羅馬投降並成為附庸王，既削弱了聯軍，也讓阿米尼烏斯的勝利在事後變成一場只贏了日耳曼人的內鬥。附庸首領塞格斯特先倒向羅馬，後來反被阿米尼烏斯囚禁，公元37年，塞格斯特的親屬連同阿米尼烏斯自己的族人刺殺了他。更早的公元1年，執政官路基烏斯·多米提烏斯·阿赫諾巴爾布斯在一次德意志集會中被高盧侍從刺殺，說明羅馬的介入從來不受歡迎。
peopleEn: Varus is the Roman protagonist of this war. He was one of the last representatives of the old Roman nobility, born into a senatorial family, holder of a series of public offices, and finally sent by Augustus to Germany to take over the administration and the military mess left by his predecessor. Once in post he re-registered the population, the land and the taxes of the whole province, and he brought with him the imperial routine of negotiating first and taxing afterwards; much of the hatred the Germans bore him came from that procedure rather than from any battlefield action. The man who actually decided the outcome was Arminius. He had served years in the Roman auxiliaries, was trained the Roman way, and knew the army's organisation, the rhythm of its duty roster, the distribution of rations and the vulnerabilities of a marching column. The Romans gave him cavalry training and even put him in charge of an auxiliary detachment, so his knowledge of Rome was that of an insider, not of a spy. Using the pretext of recruiting troops for the coalition, he obtained Roman weapons and grain, armed the tribes with Roman discipline, chose his ground, staged his attacks and walked Rome into the marsh he had selected. A second decisive figure was Marobodus, king of the Marcomanni. He refused to join the coalition, surrendered his people to Rome instead and became a client king, which weakened the coalition and turned Arminius' victory afterwards into a private quarrel among Germans. The client chieftain Segester first turned to Rome and was then thrown in chains by Arminius; in AD 37 Segester's relatives, joined by Arminius' own kinsmen, murdered him. Earlier, in AD 1, the consul Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus was killed by a Gallic servant during a gathering of the Germans, a sign that Roman involvement was never welcome.
kits: 卡面上的羅馬重步兵，在公元9年真實的裝備並不等於後世想像的那一身。分段鎧甲最早的考古實例出自萊茵河畔公元9至16年的營地，當日作戰的兵團主力防護仍是鎖子甲與鱗甲，分段鎧甲是此後數十年才逐漸普及的東西。真正決定士兵在沼澤裡生死的，是那面半圓形的重盾：直徑約一公尺二、寬約半米，邊緣包鉛，正面有球形盾心；它擋得住德意志人的投槍與砍劈，卻讓兵員在泥濘地形中無法排開，側身行軍時盾牌互相鉤連，縱隊一斷，整個方陣就散。短劍方面，羅馬人用長約半米多、寬約四公分的西班牙式短劍，刺擊為主，另配一把匕首；投射武器以約兩米長、槍桿為山毛櫸木的重標槍為主，輔以輕標槍，弓兵提供曲射火力。輔助騎兵用更長的雙刃直刀並配小圓盾，羅馬本部的百餘名騎兵只負責偵察與傳令。軍隊的另一半是輜重：帳篷、炊具、水桶、攻城器材與三十日份穀物要靠數百輛雙輪車拖行，軍中非戰鬥人員夾在縱隊之間，縱隊長度因此遠超戰鬥線。德意志戰士幾乎沒有金屬護甲，多用木盾、皮革護具與長矛，短劍形制介乎奧克西斯式與柳葉形之間；他們在卡爾克里塞的戰場上把繳獲的羅馬盾牌金屬部件拆下，改鑄成自己的首飾與馬具飾件，這些小鐵片是這場戰爭最直接的物證。
kitsEn: The Roman legionary on the card was not, in AD 9, dressed the way the later imagination dresses him. The earliest archaeological examples of segmented plate armour come from camps on the Rhine dated to AD 9 to 16; at the time of this battle the main protection of the legions was still mail and scale, and segmented plate became common only over the following decades. What actually decided whether a man lived or died in the marsh was the semicircular heavy shield: roughly one metre twenty across and half a metre wide, with leaded rims and a domed metal boss in the centre. It stopped the German spears and blows, but it meant that the men could not spread out in wet ground; when the files turned sideways the shields fouled each other, and once the column broke, the whole formation came apart. For close fighting the Romans used the Spanish-style gladius, a little over half a metre long and about four centimetres wide, aimed mainly for the thrust, together with a pugio dagger. Their missile work rested on the heavy pilum, about two metres long with an ash shaft, supported by lighter hastae, while the archers supplied the curved fire. Auxiliary horsemen carried the longer double-edged spatha with a small round shield, while the hundred-odd cavalrymen of the legions proper served as scouts and couriers. The other half of the army was its baggage: tents, cooking gear, water barrels, siege equipment and thirty days of grain dragged by several hundred two-wheeled wagons, with the non-combatants of the column travelling among them, so that the marching column stretched far beyond the fighting line. The German warriors wore almost no metal body armour; they relied on wooden shields, leather protection and long spears, and their short swords fell between the Acinaces pattern and the leaf-shaped type. On the battlefield at Kalkriese they broke the metal fittings off the Roman shields they had captured and recast them into their own ornaments and harness fittings; those small pieces of iron are the most direct physical evidence of this war.
tactics: 阿米尼烏斯沒有在開闊地上尋找正面會戰。他選擇在縱隊行軍、側翼暴露的時刻發動襲擊：德軍以鬆散隊形在森林兩側不斷騷擾，把羅馬人拖成長蛇，專打行軍縱隊的尾部與負責警戒的後衛，切斷羅馬的偵察與糧秣供應；德軍幾乎沒有騎兵，追不上羅馬的偵察騎兵，但靠散兵與林地掩蔽，足夠遲滯這支部隊。最後一戰的地形是沼澤低谷：羅馬軍必須涉過一條溪流，隊形被拉成狹長單列，兩側是泥濘的斜坡與樹林。塔西陀記載德意志人不是以密集方陣作戰，而是散開成環形包圍，不把正面交給重盾步兵；投射的長矛與石塊先消耗羅馬的輔助兵，繼而近身砍殺。瓦魯斯下令追擊退卻的敵人，羅馬步兵因而離開營地追入泥地，前後失去接應，最後被切割成數段；百夫長逐段死守，輜重隊與營帳被德軍搶掠，縱隊中的非戰鬥人員則被驅散進林地。德軍在最後攻勢中用的是最簡單也最有效的手段：從樹林與高地側翼同時壓上，切斷羅馬通往沼澤深處的通路。羅馬方面本可結盾（testudo）並嚴守縱隊接應，但沼澤地形不給結盾的空間，重盾的優勢在泥中反而成了累贅；步兵一旦脫離行列，羅馬的射擊與支援都無法覆蓋。
tacticsEn: Arminius never looked for a pitched battle in the open. He struck when the column was on the march and its flanks were exposed: the Germans harassed the flanks of the column in loose formation from the forest, stretched the Romans out into a long snake and went for the tail of the column and the rearguard on guard duty, cutting Roman scouting and resupply off. The Germans had almost no cavalry and could not catch the Roman scouts, but scattered skirmishers and the cover of the woods were enough to slow this army down. The ground of the last battle was a low marshy hollow: the Roman army had to ford a stream, the formation was drawn out into a narrow single file, with muddy slopes and woodland on both sides. Tacitus records that the Germans did not fight in a dense mass but spread out to form a ring, refusing to give the shield infantry their front; missiles and stones first wore down the Roman auxiliaries, and only then did they close in for the kill. Varus ordered a pursuit of the withdrawing enemy, and the Roman foot, following into the mud, lost contact front and rear and was finally cut into separate segments; the centurions held each segment as long as they could, while the baggage train and the tents were plundered and the non-combatants in the column were driven off into the trees. In the final attack the Germans used the simplest and most effective means available: pressure from the woodland and the high ground on the flank at the same time, shutting the Romans off from the way into the deep marsh. The Roman answer should have been the testudo and strict cohesion of the column, but the marsh gave no room for a testudo; the same heavy shield that was an advantage in the open became a liability in the mud, and once the infantry lost its order, neither Roman fire nor support could reach it.
data: 兵力：羅馬方面是三個軍團，按當時編制每團約五千五百名步兵，合計約一萬六千至一萬八千名 legionary，另有數千輔助步兵與約五千至六千名輔助騎兵，總兵力一般估計在三萬上下，偏高者估到四萬至五萬；狄奧的說法是德軍人數與羅馬相當，而德軍中相當一部分是先前列為「盟友」、站在羅馬一側的部落。損失：三個軍團全滅，史料一致認為生還者只剩數千，最多不過一萬人，被俘者依塔西陀的記載分成三批，押往不同部落出售；德軍的傷亡同樣以萬計，但聯軍主力始終保持完整，這是兩邊損失比例懸殊的關鍵。時間：公元9年9月，戰役本身約兩至三天，行軍段則持續數日。距離：羅馬軍從森林夏營到卡爾克里塞的行軍約二十五至三十公里，戰場距奧斯納布呂克約二十公里。補給：每名步兵日配穀物約一公斤，另有豆類、鹽、醃肉與葡萄酒，軍隊自攜約三十日的乾糧，因此每次宿營都要挖壕築垣、列帳。考古：1987年起，考古人員在卡爾克里塞山丘發掘出集體墓地與羅馬營地城牆的痕跡，2002年卡爾克里塞博物館正式開放，公眾得以在戰場原址看到這片沼澤的實物。
dataEn: Strength: on the Roman side, three legions at the period establishment of about five thousand five hundred foot each, giving some sixteen to eighteen thousand legionaries, plus several thousand auxiliary infantry and roughly five to six thousand auxiliary horsemen; the usual estimate for the whole force is around thirty thousand, with higher figures of forty to fifty thousand. Dio states that the German force was about equal in numbers, and a considerable part of it consisted of tribes previously standing on the Roman side as allies. Losses: all three legions were destroyed; the sources agree that only a few thousand, at most ten thousand, came back, and the prisoners were, according to Tacitus, divided into three batches and taken off to different tribes to be sold. German dead and wounded also ran into the tens of thousands, but the main body of the coalition remained intact, and that is the key to the lopsided ratio of losses. Time: September of AD 9, the fighting itself lasting about two or three days, with the marching phase spread over several days. Distances: the march from the summer camp in the forest to Kalkriese was about twenty-five to thirty kilometres, and the battlefield lay some twenty kilometres from Osnabrück. Supply: roughly one kilogram of grain per foot per day, with pulses, salt, salted meat and wine, and about thirty days of provisions carried with the army, which is why every night camp was dug and palisaded and the tents laid out in order. Archaeology: from 1987 excavators at the Kalkriese hill uncovered a mass grave and traces of the earthwork of a Roman camp, and in 2002 the Kalkriese museum opened, putting the marsh itself on public view at the site of the battle.
cause: 直接起因是奧古斯都的德意志政策。公元9年，羅馬已在威悉河與易北河之間劃出「德意志」行省，瓦魯斯接手後要做的第一件事不是打仗，而是把游牧部落變成有戶籍、有道路、有稅項的行政對象：清點人口、劃定里界、修築連接奧斯納布呂克的大道、裁決土地糾紛、徵收貢賦。對部落首領而言，這套程序意味著失去土地與裁決權，意味著傳統的武力仲裁被戶冊取代。深層原因是羅馬的軍事壓力逼出了聯軍：切羅西人、馬西人與卡蒂人不斷被要求交出人質、繳納贖金、割讓土地，羅馬的駐軍可以隨意越過邊界追捕逃奴，把森林當成巡邏的場所。阿米尼烏斯在羅馬軍中做過輔助軍軍官，熟識軍隊運作，便以為聯軍募兵的名義取得羅馬的武器、糧食與訓練，把原本鬆散的部落拼成一支有步兵協同的聯軍。聯軍選在羅馬以為安全的時間出手：墟市日。瓦魯斯必須在九日一度的市集日回到自己在奧斯納布呂克附近的莊園主持交易，行程與路線都是固定的；而這條從森林夏營通往奧斯納布呂克的路線，恰好是阿米尼烏斯最熟悉的沼澤與狹窄地帶。
causeEn: The immediate cause was Augustus' German policy. By AD 9 Rome had already marked out a province of Germany between the Weser and the Elbe, and the first thing Varus did on taking over was not to fight but to turn a roaming tribal population into an administrative one with registers, roads and taxes: counting heads, fixing boundaries, building the great road towards Osnabrück, arbitrating land disputes and levying tribute. For the chieftains this procedure meant losing their land and their jurisdiction, and seeing force-based arbitration replaced by written rolls. The deeper cause was that Roman military pressure produced the coalition in the first place. The Cherusci, Marsi and Chatti were constantly pressed for hostages, ransom and land; the Roman garrison could cross the frontier at will to chase runaways and treat the forest as a place to patrol. Arminius had been an auxiliary officer in the Roman army and knew how it worked, so under the pretext of recruiting for the coalition he obtained Roman weapons, grain and training and welded loose tribes into an infantry that could act together. The coalition struck at the moment Rome thought itself safe: the market day. Varus had to be back at his estate near Osnabrück for the nundinae, and both the timing and the route of that journey were fixed; and the road from the summer camp in the forest to Osnabrück ran through exactly the marshes and defiles that Arminius knew best.
impact: 這場戰役改變了帝國的地理。奧古斯都在消息傳到後放棄把易北河下游併入行省的計畫，把萊茵河定為帝國的永久邊界，東岸不再推進；他在遺囑中限制繼承者不得在意大利境外擴編軍隊，卻也拒絕以武力追討被俘者，採取史稱的寬恕路線，不對德意志部落進行報復。軍事的直接後果是三個軍團的編制就此消失，羅馬在萊茵以東的部署能力被清零，直到提比略與日耳曼尼庫斯在一四至一六年發動復仇遠征，奪回第十九軍團的鷹旗與其他軍旗，才在名聲上挽回一些顏面；此後羅馬放棄大規模征服，改採沿萊茵設防的守勢政策，德意志各部落在相當長的時間裡保持獨立。思想上，這場戰役從此屬於歐洲的公共記憶：塔西陀在《日耳曼尼亞志》裡稱阿米尼烏斯為無疑的日耳曼解放者，十九世紀的德國民族主義把赫爾曼塑造成民族英雄，德特莫爾德的赫爾曼紀念碑在一八七五年立起，二〇〇二年卡爾克里塞博物館在戰場原址開放。對考古學而言，沼澤的泥漿也讓這場一千八百多年前的敗仗第一次有了可供觸摸的地面證據。
impactEn: This battle changed the geography of the empire. When the news reached him, Augustus abandoned the project of annexing the lower Elbe and fixed the Rhine as the empire's permanent frontier, no longer pushing east of it. In his will he restricted his successors from raising troops outside Italy, yet he also refused to demand the prisoners back and followed what is called the policy of clemency, taking no revenge on the German tribes. The direct military consequence was the erasure of three legionary establishments; Rome's position east of the Rhine was effectively wiped out, and only the punitive expeditions of Tiberius and Germanicus in AD 14 to 16, which recovered the eagle of the Nineteenth and other standards, restored something to Roman pride. From then on Rome renounced large-scale conquest and took up a defensive policy of fortified lines along the Rhine, and the German tribes remained independent for a considerable time. In the realm of ideas the battle became part of Europe's public memory: Tacitus called Arminius the undisputed liberator of Germany in the Germania, nineteenth-century German nationalism turned Hermann into a national hero, the Hermann monument at Detmold was raised in 1875, and the Kalkriese museum opened on the battlefield itself in 2002. For archaeology, the mud of the marsh also gave this defeat of nearly two thousand years ago its first tangible ground evidence that could be touched with the hand.
result: 結果是羅馬軍隊全滅。瓦魯斯在下令突圍失敗後以自己的劍自刎，頭顱被送給阿米尼烏斯，後者據說用希臘語寫詩稱頌此事；第十九軍團的鷹旗與各軍團的標準盡落敵手，德軍把繳獲的盾牌金屬部件拆下改鑄成首飾，這些碎片今日仍在卡爾克里塞出土。兵員方面，被俘者依塔西陀的記載被分成三批押往不同部落出售，生還者不足一萬，且多半是輔助兵與軍中隨行人員，軍團的作戰骨幹幾乎沒有回來。聯軍雖然獲勝，代價同樣慘重：阿米尼烏斯原本只想把羅馬人趕出易北河，勝利後卻無法控制聯盟的野心；他與拒絕參戰的馬科曼尼王馬羅布杜斯決裂，後者早已倒向羅馬並成為附庸王，聯軍內部為誰享受戰果而裂痕叢生；公元三十七年，塞格斯特的親屬聯同阿米尼烏斯自己的族人刺殺了他，兩年後塞吉梅爾也死去。羅馬的反應不是報復性再出征，而是承認邊界：這支部隊從此退回萊茵河，此後兩個世紀裡，德意志中部沒有再出現羅馬的常駐軍團。真正的結局是兩敗俱傷：羅馬失去了三個軍團和向北擴張的夢想，德意志聯軍贏了一場戰役，卻在十年之內喪失了團結與領袖。
resultEn: The result was the annihilation of the Roman army. When his attempt to break out failed, Varus cut his own throat with his own sword; his head was carried to Arminius, who is said to have celebrated it in Greek verse. The eagle of the Nineteenth and the standards of the other legions all fell into German hands, and the Germans stripped the metal fittings from the captured shields and recast them into ornaments; those fragments are still being unearthed at Kalkriese today. In men, the prisoners were divided into three batches and sent off to different tribes for sale, according to Tacitus. Fewer than ten thousand came back, and they were for the most part auxiliaries and camp followers; virtually none of the fighting core of the legions returned. The coalition won, but it paid dearly: Arminius had only wanted the Romans out of the Elbe, and once he had won he could not control the ambitions of his partners. He quarrelled with Marobodus, king of the Marcomanni, who had refused to join the coalition and had already gone over to Rome as a client king, and the alliance split over who was to enjoy the spoils. In AD 37 Segester's relatives, together with Arminius' own kinsmen, murdered him, and two years later Segimer died as well. Rome's answer was not a war of revenge but the acceptance of a frontier: the army withdrew to the Rhine, and for two centuries no Roman garrison legion would reappear in central Germany. The true outcome was a draw between two losers: Rome lost three legions and its dream of expansion to the north, while the German coalition won a battle and within ten years lost both its cohesion and its leader.
